messages.subject: Add unmapped legend to geom_point
parts:
HI everyone,
I have a simple scatter plot and am trying to add a legend that is not mapped to either of the two variables.  I would like the legend to include "Spearman's R = x.xx" and "p=0.00x".  I can't seem to find a way to create a custom legend that isn't mapped to any variable within the plot.  BUT, now that I think about it, I wonder if I can, in the legend function, call out the R and P values from a cor.test?

Here is my code, apologies for not knowing how to do dput.  I tried messing with the order of the theme arguments thinking that perhaps they were obscuring the legend, but it didn't work, or I didn't try hard enough.  IDK.

neo_firm=ggplot(first48,aes(X6Firm15,neo6)) +
  geom_point(color="blue", size=3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm",se=TRUE) +
  labs(x="NEO (nmol/g Stool)",y="Firm. Rel. Abundance",
       title="Stool MPO and 
       Firmicutes at 6 Weeks") +
  theme(plot.title=element_text(size=16,face="bold"),
        axis.title.x=element_text(size = 14),
        axis.title.y=element_text(size = 14),
        panel.border = element_blank(),
        axis.line = element_line(size=.4),
        legend.position="bottom right",
        legend.background=element_rect(),
        legend.margin=unit(2,"cm"),
        legend.text=element_text("Spearman R = -0.394",size=10))

Thanks all!

messages.author: 8c8f0ca54c4a2459
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Add unmapped legend to geom_point
parts:
Hi Zachary,

I think what you want is what is referred to as an “annotation” in ggplot, which is separate from a legend.

... + annotate("text", x = X_LOCATION, y = Y_LOCATION, text="Spearman R = -0.394") + ...

If you want to include values from your statistical test, you can use paste() like so:

results = cor.test(SOMETHINGSOMETHING)
... + annotate("text", , x = X_LOCATION, y = Y_LOCATION, text=paste("P =", results$p.value)) + ...

You may want to wrap the results with round() or signif() to avoid excessive decimal places.

​
